items.summary: AlloyDB for PostgreSQLAnnouncementThe following AlloyDB AI functions and improvements are available inPreview:The ai.extract function lets you extract structured data fromunstructured text directly within your database queries without needingexternal extraction pipelines. For more information, seeExtract structured data.The ai.classify function lets you categorize unstructured text intopredefined labels directly within your database queries. For moreinformation, see Classify text.Parameter names and signatures for AI query engine functions(ai.analyze_sentiment, ai.summarize, and ai.agg_summarize) areupdated. For more information, seeModel endpoint reference.The prompt and prompts parameters are renamed to input andinputs in scalar and batch functions respectively.An optional additional_instructions parameter is added toai.summarize and ai.agg_summarize to provide custom instructions toguide summary formatting, length, and tone.In cursor-based versions of ai.analyze_sentiment and ai.summarize,the prompt parameter is removed.ai.agg_summarize supports multiple positional signatures, includingpassing optional additional instructions and specifying model IDs.BigQueryFeatureThe Data Engineering Agent now integrates with GoogleDrive,letting you provide Google Sheets files, CSV, or JSONL files as input foryour data engineering pipelines.This feature is generally available (GA).Cloud DNSAnnouncementStarting January 5, 2027, CNAME chasing behavior will change so that Cloud DNSfollows CNAME chains between public and private zones. If your private zones orresponse policies have overlapping domain names with public CNAME targets,queries might resolve to unintended internal IP addresses or return resolutionerrors.The following table outlines the current and updated behaviors.Source of CNAME answerCurrent behavior (until January 5, 2027)New behavior (starting January 5, 2027)Cloud DNS public zoneSubsequent queries search only public DNS zones and internal DNS. Privatezones, forwarding zones, and response policies are ignored.Subsequent queries follow the complete VPC name resolutionorder: response policies, private zones, forwarding or peering zones, internalDNS, and public zones.Cloud DNS private zoneSubsequent queries search only authorized private zones. Public DNS zones are ignored.Subsequent queries follow the complete VPC name resolutionorder. If the target isn't found in authorized private zones, Cloud DNSqueries public DNS zones.Cloud DNS response policy zoneCloud DNS systems don't perform queries for CNAME answers receivedfrom response policy local data rules.Subsequent queries follow the complete VPC name resolutionorder. If the target isn't found in response policies or private zones,Cloud DNS queries public DNS zones.Review your CNAME chasing needs before January 5, 2027. Test your DNS query pathsusing dig or nslookup to identify CNAME chasing scenarios.Look for private-to-public CNAME chasing scenarios: Look for CNAME answersfrom response policies or private zones that don't match any response policyor record in a private zone. Previously, these queries resulted in a NXDOMAINanswer but after January 5, 2027, these scenarios might match a record in apublic zone or continue to be NXDOMAIN responses.Look for public-to-private CNAME chasing scenarios: Look for CNAME answersfrom public zones that don't match any record in a public zone. Previously,these CNAME chasing scenarios would have resulted in a NXDOMAIN response.After January 5, 2027, these scenarios might match a response policy or recordin a private zone or continue to be NXDOMAIN responses if the private zonedoesn't have the record.For CNAME chasing scenarios under your control: As best practice, configurematching time-to-live (TTL) values for all records in the CNAME chain.AnnouncementStarting January 5, 2027, Cloud DNS will disable full responses to DNS queries oftype ANY (QTYPE=ANY) in public authoritative zones.Instead, a single resource record will return for ANY queries, chosen from theexisting resource record sets that match the query.Standard traffic from web browsers, applications, and API traffic query specificrecord types directly and are therefore unaffected with no action required.However, certain legacy scripts, automated health checkers, debugging commands(for example, dig example.com ANY), or custom third-party monitoring systemsthat explicitly query ANY records will receive the first available recordinstead of a full zone inventory. You must complete the following configurationupdates before January 5, 2027:Identify legacy queries: Review internal tools, deployment scripts, orthird-party DNS monitoring configurations for commands or API calls thatrequest the ANY record type.
